### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/index.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via canExport (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin), canReadObject (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin), canWriteObject (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin), getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface), canReadObject (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin), canWriteObject (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 097ef802700e109aa98a89c2991041516476b6f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7e6e4c2caf6d4cd0f209bc867e29affb5f9c3988` — the merge of head `03ae8604a894db1b7a3f36d34d9ad03904e30609` into base `097ef802700e109aa98a89c2991041516476b6f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7e6e4c2caf6d4cd0f209bc867e29affb5f9c3988 && git checkout 7e6e4c2caf6d4cd0f209bc867e29affb5f9c3988
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 097ef802700e109aa98a89c2991041516476b6f9 03ae8604a894db1b7a3f36d34d9ad03904e30609 && git checkout -B drift-repro 097ef802700e109aa98a89c2991041516476b6f9 && git merge --no-ff 03ae8604a894db1b7a3f36d34d9ad03904e30609

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 097ef802700e109aa98a89c2991041516476b6f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 097ef802700e109aa98a89c2991041516476b6f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `03ae8604a894db1b7a3f36d34d9ad03904e30609`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #21079 (body and all 12 comments through `5937906612`), PR #21217 (body, the 14-file list, the net diff `097ef802...03ae8604`, +722/−248), and the 42 check-runs on the head (38 success, 4 skipped — Auto Label and Check PR Size on one of their two runs, Console Pin Gate, the opt-in Packed-tarball smoke — 0 failure; Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core, every Type Check job, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness and Build Docs all green). Ruling E `5933054144` (maintainer 「同意E」) is the governing text; the seat's route B revision `5937041708` and revision 2 `5937093863` are the claim surface. Source positions below are git reads of the head, not runs. ⚠️ Security family: classes, positions, codes and statuses only.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set change the diff implies, each named right or wrong against the head's source:

1. **Step 2 CRUD gate, `security-plugin.ts` ~2516 — RIGHT.** The resolved-set guard is gone; the gate now runs for every non-system caller the hand-through did not admit, and a principal-carrying caller with an empty list is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 by the evaluator's answer to that list. The principal-less hand-through (`isPrincipalLessContext`, ~2216, `return next()`) and the `publicFormGrant` branch (~2043–2113, `await next()` then `return`) both precede the gate, so the ADR-0096 context and the public-form submit never reach it. The referential FK-clear exception is unchanged, and on that path step 2.6 still stands down (the narrowest answer).
2. **`canReadObject` arm 2 (~5812), `canExport` (~6201), `canWriteObject` arm 4 (~6098) — RIGHT.** Each answers `isPrincipalLessContext(context)` for an empty list. For the principal-less context the answer is unchanged (`true`; arm 4 already skipped its field arm for that context, and the organization wall is never asked without a user id). For a principal-carrying caller every answer narrows to `false`. No arm widens.
3. **`getReadFilter` (~5389, ~5422) — RIGHT.** The inline predicate it replaced (`positions.length === 0 && explicit.length === 0 && !context?.userId`) is byte-for-byte the body of `isPrincipalLessContext` (~352), so the hand-off is unchanged; the new deny-sentinel return for an empty list sits after resolution, inside the existing fail-closed `try`, and agrees with the middleware's refusal.
4. **D10 delegator arms — `canReadObject` arm 6, `canWriteObject` arm 8, the `canExport` intersection — RIGHT, and in surface.** The middleware's own D10 ask at ~2586 carries no length guard (`if (delegatorSets && !checkObjectPermission(...))`), so the three probes' length guard was a second spelling that admitted a delegator with no set while the engine refused. Dropping it narrows only. Claim revision `5937041708` records the three arms; same class, mechanical, pinned (the second-principal pair, a set-holding delegator as control), ablated one leg each.
5. **Door consequences — RIGHT, and each one the ruling ordered or its migration text names.** The app-declared `authRequired: false` endpoint: 200 → 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (authentication passed, refused at admission; the cache directive is not on the refusal). The public-form picker on a deployment without the set it names: 200 → 403 (the 5 picker pins from #21062 re-pinned under route B; the ruling's own reading gives `publicPicker` no producer and no first-party caller, so the window to #21180 costs nothing). A signed-in user on a baseline-disabled embedder: every door 403. The public-form submit: unaffected (the grant branch admits ahead of step 2; 26 stock-showcase and security dogfood files green on both legs; Dogfood Regression Gate green on the head). Fork clause: not triggered.
6. **One flip the PR names but a reader could miss — RIGHT, with no public door.** `canWriteObject` now answers the public-form grant context `false` (the grant is not one of its arms by its docblock's design: no wire caller presents the grant to the preview). The only consumer is the plugin's own write-preview hook (~1359); the public form exposes `GET /forms/:slug`, `POST …/submit` and `GET …/lookup/:field` and no validate door, so the flip reaches the unit pin in `predicate-related-read-tenant-scope.test.ts` and nothing on the wire. That pin stays a refusal (preview invalid, the related user's columns never read) and adds the probe's answer directly.
7. **Field-level answers — unchanged, as ordered.** `getReadableFields` / `getQueryableFields` / `getWritableFields` / `getMetadataReadableFields` (#20995 / #21063) keep their answers; the moved suites keep every field assertion and move only the door assertions to refusal at admission (the fold suite now also pins explain: `object_crud` denies, `allowed` false, `fls` still hidden). `checkAuthoredRowWrite` `'abstain'`, `computeLayeredRlsFilter`, step 2.6 and the step 1.5 capability gate are untouched.
8. **Public surface — `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`, docblocks only — RIGHT.** Every changed line in that file is inside a `/** … */` block: `canReadObject`'s arm list and Fails-CLOSED paragraph, `canExport`'s Fails-CLOSED paragraph, `getMetadataReadableFields`'s "why the two differ" paragraph, and a new deny-baseline paragraph on `getReadFilter`. No method, parameter, return type, key or export moves; the arm order the `canReadObject` docblock states matches the implementation's six arms. `check:api-surface`, `check:generated`, Build Docs and Spec property liveness are green on the head.
9. **Remaining zero-set spellings** (the `permissionSets.length` guards at steps 1.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 3.6, the delegator resolution and the sharing-scope resolvers) are stand-downs now dominated by step 2 for a principal-carrying caller and by the hand-through for a principal-less one — not door-specific admission copies. The new `isPrincipalLessContext` docblock's "no second spelling" sentence reads them as absent rather than dominated; comment-only, not a contract matter.

No widening anywhere in the diff. Docs: the three `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx` passages are the ones the change falsified and now state the measured answers; #21180's seat has recorded the shared file (`5937693582`).

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/21079-zero-set-deny-baseline.md` — matches what the diff publishes.** `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor` and `@objectstack/spec: minor`, BREAKING banner, `!` in the title: a runtime accept-set narrowing in `plugin-security` and a published-contract narrowing in `spec` (docblocks). `minor` for a BREAKING entry is the repo's launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`; precedents throughout `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, and the #21061 / #21063 changesets at `2bddb19c` / `665cab33`). Two packages in one changeset is well-formed; Check Changeset is green on the head.
- **`Clause-②:` line — `yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and in the changeset — RIGHT.** The spec contract's stated answers narrow; this is the #21134 precedent's spelling for a docblock-only contract narrowing and the spelling ruling E's execution parameters fix. Under the AGENTS.md grammar `yes` takes at least `minor` (held) and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING (held). The claim's bare `Clause-②: yes` (`5934758335`) is also well-formed (the arm is optional) and does not contradict it; the changeset carries the arm the gate reads.
- **ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — RIGHT.** The **Migration.** paragraph is the ruling's text verbatim and is a grant decision (declare and assign a set; resolve the `guest` anchor's bindings under #21158), not a FROM → TO rewrite of anything an author wrote: no authorable key, export, stored shape or wire shape is removed or renamed, `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to reach, and no semantic entry could detect the condition in stored metadata (a missing grant is not a shape). ADR-0087's own text draws that line — a prescription for a source-code consumer or an operator is not the ledger's business — and the gate's detector asks for a rewrite arrow or an old/new column pair and finds neither. Phase 0's N7 expectation that the marker "would be wrong under route D" predates the ruling and read the migration text as a rewrite; the two precedent changesets in this family carry the same category, and `check:adr-0087-registration` is among the 109 derived families the dev reports at exit 0.
- The migration prescription AGENTS.md requires of a breaking changeset is present, and so is the implementer note for a third-party `ISecurityService`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag (phase 0 `5929705833`, round 1 `5936988829`, patch round `5937906612`, the PR body's acceptance notes) and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated:

- **N6 (the route)** → ruled E (`5933054144`); built as route D, the deny baseline alone. Answered.
- **Q2 (whose `guest` anchor bindings on a multi-organization deployment)** → not decided; travels with #21158 (on hold). Nothing in this diff depends on it. Answered by the ruling.
- **Q3 (who edits the spec docblocks)** → A, same PR, surface declared in the claim. Answered and done.
- **Round-1 open question (two out-of-surface picker files)** → seat ruled route B (`5937041708`); re-pinned, no case deleted, and the masked-only picker pin strengthened so it discriminates (its first ablation run was a no-op leg; re-run red after `335cae74`). Answered.
- **Zone 2 assumption 4 falsified** (the picker-door case in `zero-set-masking.dogfood` turned red) → re-pinned with its fixture untouched; the ruling's serial clause gives the case to whichever of this card and #21180 lands second, and #21180's deletion wins at merge if it lands first. Answered.
- **Bounded in-place fix (the delegator arms)** → judged right in ① item 4 and recorded in the claim. Answered.
- **Clause-② spelling** and **ADR-0087 marker** → answered in ②.
- **Real `pnpm dev -- --fresh` boot NOT MEASURED this round** → acceptable: phase 0 measured 24 anonymous doors on a real stock boot with the same five-arm edit (every engine door 401 at authentication, the picker 403 `LOOKUP_NOT_PUBLIC` because the showcase declares none, the submit 201), this round measured the dogfood showcase harness on both legs, and the one addition since (the delegator arms) can only refuse. Residual, not a blocker.
- **API-key principal NOT MEASURED** → reasoned, not measured: it carries a user id, so the stock baseline applies and it is outside the class on `objectstack serve`; it joins the class only on a baseline-disabled embedder, which the migration text already covers. Residual, not a blocker.
- **Misleading preview message (carrier: none)** → ESCALATED to the seat: existing behaviour for every refused caller and diagnostic text only, so not a blocker here, but a finding with no carrier should be filed or given one; this PR only adds callers to the class that sees it.
- **Stale `rest-server.ts` fail-stance docblock** → carrier #21180, which edits that file. Answered.
- **Attribution form, `main` merged twice without rebase, the peek ref created and deleted** → process notes under AGENTS.md, not contract matters. Answered.
- **#21180's pointer (`forms.mdx` is a fourth shared file)** → recorded on both cards; whichever lands second removes the picker prose. Answered.
- **Raise rule / fork clause** → not triggered on either measurement; p1 stands. Answered.

Disclosure discipline held in the PR body, the changeset and the pins: classes, positions, codes and statuses; no pin title states a request.
